Do not eat for 2 h before and 1 h after; avoid grapefruit
Can cause fetal harm - contraindicated; use contraception

Mild-moderate: no adjustment; severe not studied
Mild-moderate: start 80 mg; severe not recommended
Blood pressure, bleeding, GI perforation/fistula, proteinuria, LFTs
summary: Cabozantinib (COMETRIQ capsules) is an oral multi-targeted receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor of RET, MET, VEGFR-1/2/3, KIT, AXL and others, indicated for progressive, metastatic medullary thyroid cancer. The recommended dose is 140 mg once daily on an empty stomach. Major hazards - emphasized in the label warnings - are serious and sometimes fatal hemorrhage and gastrointestinal perforations and fistulas; cabozantinib must not be given to patients with recent significant hemorrhage and must be withheld around surgery. Other key toxicities include thromboembolism, hypertension/hypertensive crisis, osteonecrosis of the jaw, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, proteinuria, diarrhea and reversible posterior leukoencephalopathy. It is a CYP3A4 substrate requiring dose adjustment with strong inhibitors or inducers.
indications: Treatment of patients with progressive, metastatic medullary thyroid cancer (MTC)

dosage.c: Progressive metastatic medullary thyroid cancer (COMETRIQ capsules)
dosage.d: 140 mg orally once daily without food
dosage.t: Once daily until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
dosage.n: Do NOT substitute COMETRIQ capsules with cabozantinib (CABOMETYX) tablets - they are not bioequivalent

dosage.d: Reduce daily dose by 40 mg (e.g., 140 mg to 100 mg); resume prior dose 2-3 days after stopping inhibitor
Increase daily dose by 40 mg (e.g., 140 mg to 180 mg), not exceeding 180 mg; resume prior dose 2-3 days after stopping inducer

dosage.c: Adverse reactions (Grade 3+ non-heme, Grade 4 heme, intolerable Grade 2)
dosage.d: Withhold; on recovery reduce stepwise (140 to 100 to 60 mg daily)
dosage.n: Permanently discontinue for GI perforation, Grade 4 fistula, severe hemorrhage, MI/serious thromboembolism, nephrotic syndrome, RPLS, or uncontrolled/Grade 4 hypertension

admin: Swallow capsules whole on an empty stomach - do not open the capsules
Do not eat for at least 2 hours before and at least 1 hour after the dose
Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice and CYP3A4-inhibiting supplements
Do not take a missed dose within 12 hours of the next dose
Withhold for at least 3 weeks before elective surgery and resume only after adequate wound healing (at least 2 weeks after major surgery)
Withhold at least 3 weeks before invasive dental procedures
moa: Cabozantinib inhibits the tyrosine kinase activity of multiple receptors including RET, MET, VEGFR-1, -2 and -3, KIT, TRKB, FLT-3, AXL, ROS1, TYRO3, MER and TIE-2. These kinases drive oncogenesis, metastasis, tumor angiogenesis, drug resistance, and maintenance of the tumor microenvironment; their inhibition reduces tumor growth and angiogenesis.

absolute: No contraindications are listed in the product labeling
relative: Recent history of serious hemorrhage or hemoptysis (do not administer)
Recent or planned major surgery / unhealed wounds
monitor: Signs of GI perforation or fistula and bleeding

preg: Can cause fetal harm based on animal data and mechanism of action; cabozantinib caused embryofetal lethality and structural anomalies in rats and rabbits at exposures below the clinical dose. Verify pregnancy status before starting; advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during and for some time after treatment, and males with female partners likewise.
lact: Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed child, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for an appropriate period after the last dose.
renal: No dosage adjustment is recommended for mild to moderate renal impairment. Cabozantinib has not been studied in severe renal impairment.
hepatic: For mild or moderate hepatic impairment, reduce the starting dose to 80 mg once daily. Use in severe hepatic impairment is not recommended.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir and other protease inhibitors, voriconazole, nefazodone) - raise cabozantinib exposure; avoid or reduce dose by 40 mg
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, rifabutin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, St John's wort) - lower cabozantinib exposure; avoid or increase dose by 40 mg
moderate: Other agents increasing bleeding risk (anticoagulants, antiplatelets) - additive hemorrhage risk
Antihypertensive needs may change due to drug-induced hypertension
minor: Drugs affecting QT or electrolytes - monitor in context of GI losses
interactions.food: Take on an empty stomach (a high-fat meal raises Cmax/AUC by 41%/57%). Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction reported; general caution.
interactions.diagnostics: May increase AST/ALT, alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin; cause hypocalcemia, hypophosphatemia, lymphopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, and proteinuria.

serious: Arterial and venous thromboembolic events (MI, stroke, PE)
emergency: Acute abdomen from GI perforation or fistula
Acute MI, stroke or pulmonary embolism
RPLS (severe headache, seizures, visual disturbance, confusion)

monitoring: Symptoms of bleeding and GI perforation/fistula
Liver function tests and serum calcium/phosphate
CBC for cytopenias; wound healing around surgery; oral/dental status for ONJ
counsel: Take the capsules whole on an empty stomach - nothing to eat 2 hours before and 1 hour after
Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit products and tell your doctor about all other medicines
Report any bleeding, black/bloody stools, severe abdominal pain, chest pain, breathlessness, or severe headache/vision changes immediately
Tell the team before any surgery or dental procedure - the drug must be stopped beforehand
Use effective contraception; this drug can harm an unborn baby - do not breastfeed
pk: Steady state reached by about day 15 of daily dosing
Median Tmax 2-5 hours after an oral dose
Once-daily dosing; 4-5 fold accumulation over 19 days
Store at controlled room temperature per labeling; keep in original packaging
pearls: Boxed/labeled key risks: serious or fatal HEMORRHAGE and GI PERFORATION/FISTULA - do not start with recent significant bleeding and hold around surgery
COMETRIQ capsules and CABOMETYX tablets are NOT interchangeable - do not substitute
Strict empty-stomach dosing and grapefruit avoidance are essential for predictable exposure
Adjust dose by 40 mg up or down for strong CYP3A4 inducers or inhibitors
Monitor and aggressively manage hypertension; watch for hand-foot syndrome and proteinuria
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless the next dose is due within 12 hours - in that case skip the missed dose. Do not take two doses to make up for a missed one.
overdose: Limited data: a patient who took twice the dose (200 mg daily) for nine days developed Grade 3 memory impairment, mental status and cognitive changes, weight loss, and raised BUN. There is no specific antidote; stop the drug and provide supportive care with monitoring of organ function.
